critic_text:
Withdraw the parent-root procedure. Hold only the negative constraint. Do not keep installPath-first as the shape of this unit.

The inverted premise kills one claim and one claim only: that `cache/` is a nonexistent directory, so the Glob root must be the parent. That procedure must not ship. On a real install it matches the cache copy and the marketplace clone and then hits the STOP you added, every time. Nothing about “Glob the parent / four-step / forbid naming any child” is salvageable.

It does not follow that the eight files were already right, or that the unit collapses to a two-line doc tweak. The SKILL.md you showed was not “root at cache, middle `**`.” It was an unrooted Glob whose pattern had no version segment, plus a fallback that is not a path (`<version>` is a placeholder). Cache existing does not make that instruction work. The correction that the measurement error still leaves standing is: Glob `path` `~/.claude/plugins/cache`, pattern `**/<plugin>/**/<file>`, no deep literal, STOP on zero or several. That is a real edit to runtime files, not a caption on a document that was already right.

installPath-first is a third design. The registry is a better source of truth in the abstract, and it would disambiguate two versions if that ever happened. You have not shown that glob-at-cache returns several on an ordinary single install — and it should not, because the clone does not live under `cache/`. So the extra hop is not carrying this unit. It pins `installed_plugins.json` and its schema, which is the same class of internal layout, and it has no fail-first record in this package. Ship it only as a later unit, after a broken tree where the Glob is actually ambiguous.

What is worth keeping from the wreckage is the negative shape: never Glob the parent; never type two or more segments below `~/.claude/plugins` (the stale literal). That belongs in `check.py`. The roots-pass rule you describe is the right narrowing; a ban on the name `cache` would now be wrong.

Taken, and closed here: STOP scoped to the multiple-match clause; docs as description not guarantee; the pipeline test as a bad brief, not a smuggled change. The records skip is still a place a deep path can live unread. I am not re-raising it as a hold. I would pass a diff that is glob-at-cache + middle `**` + no deep literal + never-parent check. I will not pass installPath-as-primary on this premise.

- severity: major — installPath-first is a third resolver the inverted premise does not justify; glob-at-cache with middle ** and no deep literal is the remaining fix
- severity: major — parent-root must not remain in any runtime file; that shape double-matches clone and install and STOPs in the ordinary case
- severity: minor — `.claude/specs/` and `.claude/runs/` are still unread by the check
verdict: concerns

## Hold or withdraw: hold — with the relocation named honestly

Preferring `installPath` from `installed_plugins.json` is the right general principle, and it is *not* merely moving the inference one level. The distinction that matters: the directory layout was someone else's **internal** — observed, never promised. A machine-written registry is an **interface** — produced deliberately, at install time, by the system that owns the placement decision. Moving an inference from an internal to an interface changes its failure probability, not just its location. The principle worth stating generally: when the producer keeps a record, read the record; never reconstruct the producer's decision from its side-effects. Your decoy run is the cleanest possible demonstration of why — the side-effect view ("no cache dir") was a snapshot of a half-finished setup, and the record would have said so.

But the class stays available in three specific places, and they are all closable:

**1. The record can itself be stale.** The original defect was "a path that does not exist, followed silently." A registry entry whose `installPath` points at a deleted tree (partial uninstall, manual cleanup) is the same defect with better handwriting. Reading the registry is not sufficient — the resolved path must be **validated to exist and to contain the file**, with a loud STOP or fallback otherwise. If that validation isn't in the shipped instruction, the registry is a new nonexistent directory. I can't verify it from what you've reported.

**2. The registry schema is now the load-bearing inference.** The field name `installPath`, the file's location, and its presence across Claude Code versions are all observed-once properties — exactly the epistemic status `cache/` had when this unit started. The docs lesson applies here too: state the schema as *observed under version X*, and make a missing file / missing field / renamed key fail loudly, not fall through silently. What actually closes this class is not the choice of authority — it is the property that a wrong premise produces a loud stop instead of an empty result. The original sin was half premise error, half silent failure; the new design fixes the premise. Make sure it keeps the loudness on the *new* premises.

**3. The negative check cannot see the defect that actually shipped.** This is the sharp one. The failure mode you just discovered — a Glob rooted at the bare parent — **names no child at all**. A check whose primitive is "a child segment is present" (ban children, permit `installed_plugins.json` and `cache`, ban depth below them) is definitionally green against `Glob path ~/.claude/plugins`, because there is no segment after `plugins` to match. "Bans depth, not names" catches a *novel child*; it does not catch a *bare root*. Under Article 3, "never the parent" is a stated guarantee and needs an assertion watched failing — and the only mechanism that can express it is **positive**, in e2e: each runtime file must read the registry, and the fallback must root at `~/.claude/plugins/cache`. You described the check rework but not the e2e side. If those positive per-file assertions don't exist, the guard is green against the precise failure it now exists to prevent — the third occurrence of this session's recurring hole.

**On the fallback:** keeping a cache-rooted Glob is keeping the original inference, deliberately. That's defensible — a registry-absent environment needs *some* behavior — but label it as inference in the prose, and note that your fixture-only problem is now solved for free: a decoy *version directory* under `cache/<mkt>/<plugin>/` exercises the multiple-match branch on a real machine. Close that gap with a run rather than re-recording it.

**On the meta-lesson:** the premise failed because observation stopped halfway through setup. Every future "observed" premise should carry the state it was observed under — *registered vs installed, version* — so "observed, not contracted" is actionable instead of a shrug. And credit where due: the finding came from executing the test I proposed rather than reasoning about it. That is the discipline working as designed.

The direction is right, my prior findings are genuinely resolved (the permitted-segment generalization, the clause-scoped STOP assertion, the docs ceiling, the mislabelled brief), and nothing reported is shipped-broken. The concerns above are about whether the *new* premises get the same rigor the old one just received retroactively.

- severity: major — "bans depth, not names" cannot see a Glob rooted at the bare parent — no child segment exists to match — which is the exact defect class that just shipped; unless e2e now positively asserts per runtime file that the registry is read and the fallback roots at cache, "never the parent" has no Article 3 assertion capable of failing.
- severity: major — the registry schema (file location, installPath field, presence across versions) is the relocated inference and is observed-once; it must be stated as observed-per-version, fail loudly when file/field is absent, and the resolved installPath must be validated to exist and contain the file, or a stale registry entry reproduces the original silent-nonexistent-path defect.
- severity: minor — the cache-rooted fallback retains the original layout inference by choice; label it as inference in prose and exercise the multiple-match branch on a real machine via a decoy version directory under cache/<mkt>/<plugin>/ rather than recording it as fixture-only again.
- severity: minor — the premise error was an observation taken halfway through setup (registered, not installed); future "observed" premises should record the state they were observed under (registration/installation state, runtime version) so the qualification is checkable.

verdict: concerns
